title: Formal verification of neural network behavior
bottleneck: Formal verification — mathematical proof that a system satisfies a specification — works for small networks but faces exponential blowup at frontier scale; verifying even modest properties of a billion-parameter model is computationally infeasible. Neural networks are also the wrong shape for verification: their behavior is defined by millions of uninterpretable weights, not logic amenable to proof. The gap between verification theory and deployed models is enormous.
why_it_blocks: High-assurance domains like aviation, medicine, and critical infrastructure require guarantees, not test scores. Without verification, AI stays out of the settings where reliability matters most.
current_state: Verification tools handle networks with thousands of neurons. Frontier models have trillions of parameters — verification is not on a credible scaling path.
